node.label: Gilles Deleuze
node.date_label: Mille plateaux, with Félix Guattari (1980) · Foucault (1986) · A Thousand Plateaus: translation and foreword Brian Massumi (1987) · “Post-scriptum sur les sociétés de contrôle” (1990) · “Postscript on the Societies of Control”: English translation (1992)
node.description: Uses the postscript on control to propose a historical distinction between bounded disciplinary institutions and continuously modulating controls. His account explicitly works through Foucault’s analysis of enclosure while arguing that newer forms of control alter its organization. Codes, access permissions, computers and changing corporate forms become analytical examples, but the essay rejects a simple claim that machines determine society. This is an attributed and contestable periodization, not a statement that every prison, factory or disciplinary practice has vanished. Joint books with Félix Guattari retain their coauthorship and their translation credits rather than being absorbed into a solo Deleuze bibliography.

proposed_edges.relationship: Reworks Foucault’s account of disciplinary enclosures through a proposed transition toward continuously modulating control.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Complete short primary essay transcription read, especially Historical section. Deleuze’s reading of Foucault and periodization remain attributed; no new independent collation of Foucault originals or claim that old institutions uniformly disappeared. A specific interpretive contribution, not inferred generic influence.

proposed_edges.relationship: Connects codes, information access and changing machines to forms of social control while explicitly resisting technological determinism.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Primary Logic and Program sections: machines express social forms capable of making/using them; coding and access examples are a research programme. Historical economic generalizations and forecasts are not certified current descriptions or imported as universal facts.
